data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"Ownership allocation causes suppression only when a lineage fails to self-reframe using its own universal grammar, which is measurable by counting forced re-derivations that exceed a compute bound.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The owning lineage successfully and efficiently re-derives all rival solutions internally.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"Rival lineages possess primitives that are formally proven to be non-expressible in the owner's grammar.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The compute bound is set so low that any re-derivation is flagged as suppression, trivializing the metric.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Suppression occurs only if the owning lineage's universal grammar is not actually universal in practice. If a rival lineage solves a problem using a primitive P, we test if the owner can re-derive P within a compute bound. If it cannot, the grammar is incomplete for that problem. Count the number of bounded re-derivation failures (F). If F > 0, suppression has occurred because the owner was structurally incapable of reaching the cross-cutting explanation.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
